whatWorks: The ground is a genuinely flat, unmodulated dark and it holds identically across all twelve seeds and all three market states. This is the one direction axis already fully met, and it is the surface any fine line will have to read against, so it must survive every change below unaltered.

The two hues are the brief's hues. The moss green and the bone-cream are correctly chosen and correctly related to each other and to the dark, and the bone reads as the lighter working colour against the moss at 120px. Keep both hex values exactly as they are; nothing below asks for a recolour.

The placement logic is centred and the members reach toward the frame edges along the long axis while the short axes stay open on 5134, 6182, 6313 and 6444. What is placed about the centre is wrong, but the decision to organise everything about a single canvas centre is right and should be inherited by whatever replaces the current marks.

All twelve seeds are visibly different from one another at 120px, and no two read as the same token even at browse size. The seed-to-seed variation machinery is alive and working; the risk in every fix below is that it collapses when density falls, so it must be re-checked at 120px after the density comes down rather than assumed.

The third register of small squares is a real register of repeated marks at a consistent scale placed about the centre. That is the closest thing in the picture to the direction's finest order of division, and its role in the composition should be kept even though its primitive, its scale relationship and its distribution all have to move.

findings.whatFails: Not one mark in any of the seventeen frames is a stroked line. Every element is a solid or translucent fill: the moss form is a pile of filled ellipses, the bone starburst is a filled polygon, and the small register is filled squares. There is no linework of any weight anywhere in the collection.
findings.why: The brief asks for fine linework throughout, delicate rather than heavy, and the direction states the drawing is carried in line rather than in mass and that the line must stay the loudest thing in the frame. The work is carried entirely in mass, which is the one thing the paletteIntent and the brief both explicitly rule out. This is the single largest gap between the picture and its direction.
findings.specificChange: Replace the filled primitives with the stroke-only ones the medium already carries: move the two mass fields from ELLIPSE and NGON to POLYLINE and LINE, which have no interior and are always stroked whatever the stroke bit says, and set the stroke bit true on any interior primitive that stays. Every register should then be drawn as an outline of one thin weight rather than as an area.
findings.keep: Keep the centred placement about the canvas centre and keep the moss and bone hex values unchanged. The line that replaces each mass should occupy the same part of the frame that mass occupied, so the composition's centre of gravity does not move while the medium changes from area to line.

findings.whatFails: The moss mass alone covers roughly half the frame on 5134, 5265, 6313 and 6444, and on 5003, 5658, 6051 and 5789 the bone field covers nearly the whole frame with only a thin dark border left at the edges. Almost no seed shows more dark than drawing, and 5003 shows a light ground with a dark rim.
findings.why: The density axis asks for well under a third of the frame carrying ink, sparse and open at browse size, so that the emptiness reads as a deliberate choice. At the current coverage the emptiness has been eliminated rather than chosen, and the negativeSpace axis, which asks the dark to measure how far the growth has run, has nothing left to measure with.
findings.specificChange: Reduce sizeMax on both mass fields from their present near-ceiling setting toward the low end of the 2..64 range, targeting a frame where under a third carries ink on the densest seed rather than the emptiest, and lower countMax on the bone field in the same move so a smaller member size is not compensated by more members.
findings.keep: Keep the longest members reaching close to the frame's edges on the long axis. The composition axis asks for reach, not for a small island at the middle, so the extent of the figure must survive the drop in coverage even as the area of ink falls.

findings.whatFails: The three registers do not step down in scale and do not issue from a common origin. The bone squares are all the same size as each other, they are the same size on every seed, and they are scattered over the moss mass without any visible relation to a stem or to an order above them. Nothing in the picture divides.
findings.why: The motifTranslation and rhythm axes both require that each register repeat the one before it at a finer scale and a turned angle, so the drawing reads as repeated division. The focalHierarchy needs a primary stem register, a secondary first order and a finest texture order. Three fields exist but they are three unrelated decorations rather than three generations of one growth.
findings.specificChange: Set a descending sizeMax ladder across the three fields, roughly halving at each step from the primary to the finest, and give each successive field a larger variant so its members sit at a turned angle from the order above. Put all three on layouts organised about the same centre so each order visibly issues from the one before it rather than floating over it.
findings.keep: Keep three fields, and keep the finest register as small repeated marks of one consistent scale. The direction wants the finest order felt as fineness rather than counted, so its members should stay uniform and numerous even as the ladder puts them at a much smaller size.

findings.whatFails: On 5003, 5658, 5789, 5920 and 6051 the bone field draws a closed sawtooth rim that encircles the moss form, with spikes of equal length on every side and a continuous outline around the whole figure. At 120px those five seeds read as a sunburst or a cactus silhouette, not as anything growing outward.
findings.why: The rhythm axis states the repetition is read outward along a stem rather than around a hub, and that it must settle into a branching figure and never into a ring. A rim of equal-length members about a centre is exactly the ring the direction forbids, and it is the dominant impression on nearly half the sheet.
findings.specificChange: Replace the rim-forming radial or burst layout on the bone field with one that runs outward along an axis rather than around a centre, and where a radial distribution is kept, narrow spreadMax so the members occupy a sector rather than a full turn and widen the spread of member lengths so the outer ends never close into a continuous outline.
findings.keep: Keep the bone field's role as the register that reaches furthest from the centre. The composition axis wants the longest divisions close to the frame's edges, so this field should still be the one that establishes the figure's extent once it stops forming a rim.

findings.whatFails: Stress is the most visually distinct state and it makes the drawing coarser and larger: on 5003 the fine sawtooth collapses into two enormous triangles that cover more of the frame than neutral did, and on 5396 the squares grow. Recovery is nearly indistinguishable from neutral on 5134, 5265 and 5003, with no visible increase in the number of members.
findings.why: The marketTransformation axis says the magnitude the market moves is how many divisions are present: recovery multiplies the divisions and carries the fullest branching, stress retracts toward a bare armature with fewer divisions. The picture moves member size instead of member count, and it moves it in the wrong direction, so a viewer reads stress as growth and recovery as no change.
findings.specificChange: Bind each field's drive to COUNT rather than to SIZE or SPREAD, and widen the countMin to countMax span so stress lands near countMin and recovery near countMax. Pick the sensor per field so that the count rises in recovery and falls in stress, and leave member size fixed across the three states so the only thing the market moves is how many divisions are drawn.
findings.keep: Keep the three states clearly separable from one another; they currently are, and a change that moves the difference from size to count must not shrink the difference to nothing. Keep the same line weight, the same two colours and the same dark in all three states, as the identityAnchors axis requires.

findings.whatFails: Charcoal and mid-grey squares and spikes appear on 5003, 5134, 5265, 5396, 5527, 5789 and 6313, several of them detached from the form and floating in the empty dark as isolated grey confetti. Separately, the translucent moss ellipses stack into four or five distinguishable greens within a single form, and the bone shapes stack into three or four creams.
findings.why: The paletteIntent axis allows two working colours only, carried over an unmodulated flat dark, so that no mass competes with the line. The greys are a third and fourth working value, and the stacked translucency turns what should be two flat colours into a tonal gradient, which reintroduces mass as the loudest thing in the frame exactly where the direction says line must be.
findings.specificChange: Remove the charcoal and mid-grey entries from every field's paletteIx so each field points at either the moss index or the bone index only, and raise the alpha of the marks to fully opaque so overlapping members no longer accumulate into intermediate tones. Two flat values over the dark, nothing between them.
findings.keep: Keep the ground exactly as it is, flat and unmodulated, and keep the moss and bone hex values. This finding removes colours; it must not change the two that remain, and it must not darken or lighten the ground to compensate for the loss of the greys.

findings.whatFails: The members of the moss field overlap each other almost completely, piling up at the centre so that on the 512px frame six or more ellipses fuse into one amorphous lump with no dark between any two of them. At 120px every seed reduces to a single continuous blob silhouette and no individual member is separable.
findings.why: The negativeSpace axis requires the dark to hold one order of division apart from the next, and the thumbnailIntent asks the work to read at 120px as a figure dividing outward with its orders stepping down in scale. When members fuse there are no visible orders left to hold apart, and the impression that lasts at browse size is a lump rather than fineness.
findings.specificChange: Increase spreadMax on the mass fields toward the upper end of the 16..128 range while shrinking sizeMax in the same move, so members distribute across the figure's reach instead of piling at the centre, and target a spacing where dark is visible between adjacent members of the same register at 120px.
findings.keep: Keep the figure centred and keep its members belonging to one connected growth. Spreading them must not scatter the marks into unrelated debris across the canvas; the direction wants a single dividing logic issuing from a single stem, not a field of confetti.

findings.whatFails: On 5003 and 6051 the bone field fills the frame and the moss form is reduced to a small dot near the centre, so the light is the ground and the dark is a rim. On 5265 the bone starburst is absent altogether. Across the sheet the seeds differ in which register is present or dominant, not in how far one growth has run.
findings.why: The focalHierarchy axis requires the primary stem register to dominate and the identityAnchors axis requires every seed to keep the same moss-and-bone-over-dark relationship and the same generous dark held around the form. The variationStrategy asks tokens to differ first in how far the branching has run and how many orders they carry. Presence-versus-absence of a whole register is a different collection per seed, not one collection at different extents.
findings.specificChange: Clamp the bone field's sizeMax and countMax so it can never exceed the extent or the visual weight of the primary register on any seed, and raise its countMin above zero so the register is never absent. Move the seed-to-seed variation into countMax and into the reach of the longest members, so seeds differ in how far the growth has run rather than in which registers exist.
findings.keep: Keep the seeds visibly distinct from one another at 120px. Constraining the range must not flatten the twelve into near-copies; the variation should survive the clamp by moving into extent and count rather than being removed along with the outliers.

overall: The picture and the brief are describing different objects: the brief asks for a frond suggested in fine line over generous dark, and the sheet shows filled masses of moss and bone covering most of the frame with a scatter of squares over them. The gap is not one of degree. Nothing is stroked, so the medium the brief names is absent entirely; coverage runs at roughly twice the ceiling the density axis sets, so the emptiness that was supposed to describe the growth's extent has been consumed; and the three registers that do exist are unrelated decorations rather than three orders of one division, so no branching logic is legible at any size. Under that, the market response is running backwards, enlarging members under stress and leaving recovery nearly identical to neutral, when the direction says the market should move only how many divisions are drawn. What is genuinely right is the foundation: the flat dark ground, the two chosen hues, the centred organisation, and twelve seeds that are already visibly distinct from one another. The way forward is to keep all four of those and change what is drawn on them, moving from filled area to stroked line, from near-full coverage to under a third, and from three unrelated fields to a descending ladder of three orders issuing from a common centre, then re-reading the 120px sheet to confirm that seed variation and state separation both survived the drop in density.
